review.algorithm_assessment: Safe positions satisfy a^b<n. For a>=2 the game is finite; descending DP marks a position winning iff a safe increment reaches a losing position. Exponent>=2 has only O(sqrt(n)) total-scale base ranges, while the long b=1 tail permits only base increments and is solved by parity. At a=1, arbitrarily increasing b eventually allows an infinite draw; propagate win/loss/draw backward instead of imposing a false finite cutoff.
review.limitations: One source reviewer plus actual isolated tests, not independent dual semantic review.
